Report_ID: Recognition of depression (depression scenario) at 6-month follow-up
Title: Effectiveness of the Mental Health First Aid programme for general nursing students in Hong Kong: A randomised controlled trial
Author: Hung, M.S.Y.; Chow, M.C.M.; Chien, W.T.; Wong, P.Y.K.
Comment: Outcome reported as a continuous vignette recognition score, NOT as a proportion/count correctly identifying depression; no arm-level event counts or percentages are given, so deriving an odds ratio requires the SMD -> log OR conversion (log OR = SMD x pi/sqrt(3)) flagged in the plan. Group Ns entered are the numbers RANDOMISED (182 experimental, 176 control) because the analysis was intention-to-treat with last-observation-carried-forward imputation and Table 2 does not state per-cell analysed Ns; completers at follow-up were 167 and 165 respectively. F(2,355)=36.56 and partial eta squared=0.17 are the omnibus time*group interaction across all three time points, not a follow-up-only contrast; p reported only as p<0.01. The instrument's maximum score is not stated, so no scale range was recorded. Table 2 Cohen's d values (-1.10 pre-post, -1.46 pre-follow-up) are within-group pre-vs-later comparisons with a negative sign convention for improvement, not between-group follow-up effect sizes, so they were not entered as the between-group effect size. M_diff not computed because means come from a 2x3 mixed factorial repeated-measures ANOVA.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Experimental group – 12-hour face-to-face MHFA training (Hong Kong version)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Design Type: waitlist-controlled randomised controlled trial (pre-test, post-test, 6-month follow-up)
domain: mental health literacy / Mental Health First Aid training
Medium: Face-to-face small-group interactive training with Chinese MHFA manual
Content length: 12-hour MHFA programme: four 3-hour sessions over one month
Topic of Content: Mental Health First Aid (recognition of depression, psychosis, anxiety; ALGEE action plan)
Recruitment source: One of the largest tertiary institutions in Hong Kong (class announcements and emails, April–May 2017)
Outcome measurement: Mean (SD) recognition-of-depression score at the six-month follow-up assessment, per group
Outcome variable: Recognition of depression (depression scenario) at 6-month follow-up
outcome_family: correct recognition of depression in a case vignette

Report_ID: Recognition of depression in the 'Jenny' vignette (% correct) at 6-month follow-up, teachers
Title: Mental health first aid training for high school teachers: a cluster randomized trial
Author: Jorm AF, Kitchener BA, Sawyer MG, Scales H, Cvetkovski S
Comment: The OR 3.09 (95% CI 0.77-12.43) is the pre vs follow-up by intervention interaction from a mixed-effects logistic model that accounts for clustering within schools and baseline, i.e. the cluster-adjusted estimate preferred by the plan. Per-arm numbers analysed at 6-month follow-up are NOT reported (28% of teachers did not complete the follow-up questionnaire), so the numbers randomised/analysed at baseline (221 intervention, 106 control) are recorded and the arm percentages are given without usable denominators; event counts therefore not extracted. The paper names no effect measure beyond 'OR' in the table header, and no p-value is given for this row (not flagged as significant).; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Intervention schools - immediate modified Youth Mental Health First Aid training (teachers)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
domain: mental health first aid training / mental health literacy
Participant type: High school teachers of Years 8-10 (ages 12-15 students) in South Australian schools
Recruitment source: Government, Catholic and independent high schools in South Australia
Outcome measurement: Percentage of teachers correctly naming depression; cluster-adjusted odds ratio for the pre vs follow-up by intervention interaction from a mixed-effects logistic model
Outcome variable: Recognition of depression in the 'Jenny' vignette (% correct) at 6-month follow-up, teachers
outcome_family: correct recognition of depression in a case vignette

Report_ID: Recognition of depression (% correct) at 6-month follow up
Title: Mental health first aid training by e-learning: a randomized controlled trial
Author: Jorm, Kitchener, Fischer & Cvetkovski
Comment: No inferential statistic is available: the authors report 'NA' for the depression-recognition intervention interaction because of a baseline ceiling effect. Only arm-level percentages are reported; no event counts and no per-arm numbers analysed at 6-month follow up are stated verbatim (only overall N=262 randomised across three arms and 13% non-completion of the follow-up questionnaire). Odds ratio, SE, and combined-training-arm counts were therefore NOT computed, as the required denominators are not explicitly reported.; n_treatment(131) and n_control(131) assumed equal split from n_total=262; d from proportions via OR (p_treatment=0.9700, p_control=0.9360, OR=2.2108); assumes binary outcome
Design Type: randomized controlled trial (three-arm, individually randomized, parallel)
domain: mental health literacy / Mental Health First Aid training
Study Environment: online/remote (self-administered e-learning CD or manual; web-based questionnaires)
Participant type: Adult members of the Australian general public with computer and internet access
Recruitment source: Online advertisements on community and research notice boards, flyers in university libraries and community/mental health centres, local newspaper and newsletter advertisements
Outcome measurement: Percentage of participants in each arm correctly identifying depression in the vignette at the 6-month follow-up questionnaire
Outcome variable: Recognition of depression (% correct) at 6-month follow up
additional_group_ns: Third arm (second MHFA training arm) = printed MHFA manual: 94.8% correct recognition of depression at 6-month follow up (pre 89.8, post 96.3). Per the synthesis plan the CD and manual arms would be combined into one training group, but per-arm numbers analysed at follow up are not reported in the text or extractable from the CONSORT figure, so only arm percentages are recorded here.
outcome_family: correct recognition of depression in a case vignette

Report_ID: Correct recognition of depression in the depression vignette at 6-month follow-up
Title: Effectiveness of Mental Health First Aid Training in Sweden. A Randomized Controlled Trial with a Six-Month and Two-Year Follow-Up
Author: Svensson & Hansson
Comment: NO EXTRACTABLE EFFECT: vignette recognition of depression was measured per the Methods but its results are never reported (absent from Table 2 and from all Results text) — no counts, percentages, means, F, p, OR or effect size exist for it, so no log OR / SE can be computed. Group Ns given are the numbers randomised (199 vs 207); at six months 64 experimental and 65 control participants did not complete the questionnaires, and intention-to-treat analyses used multiple imputation. Note also that Table 2's header reads "Exp. Group (n = 100)", inconsistent with the n=199 randomised, apparently a typographical error. This row is recorded only to document the outcome's unreported status; it contributes no usable data point to the pooled odds ratio.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Experimental group: 12-hour MHFA training delivered immediately') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False); unsupported or insufficient statistic type

Participant type: Public sector employees (social insurance agency, employment agencies, social services, schools, police, correctional treatment units, rescue services, recreation centres) in a county in western Sweden
Recruitment source: Staff offered MHFA training via a local coordinating organisation (Suicide Prevention In the West, SPIV)
Outcome measurement: Recognition of a disorder in vignettes describing a person with depression or schizophrenia (vignettes given alternately to participants)

Title: Effectiveness of Mental Health First Aid training in Denmark: a randomized trial in waitlist design
Author: Jensen, Morthorst, Vendsborg, Hjorthøj, Nordentoft
Comment: Only percentages with 95% CIs are reported, not raw event counts; event counts would have to be derived (72.0% of 142 ≈ 102; 60.3% of 132 ≈ 80) and were therefore not recorded as explicit counts. Ns (142/132) are the Table 2 analysis Ns for the depression-vignette subsample under an intention-to-treat analysis with multiple imputation (attrition was 40% intervention / 29% control). Outcome measurement: Percentage of participants correctly recognising the illness depicted in the depression vignette (yes/no item), with odds ratio for intervention vs control
